draft.title: Continuity and change
card: something that stays the same, or mostly the same, over a period of time.
something that becomes different over a period of time.
Most periods of history have both. A new ruler may take power while people keep farming in the way their families always have.
To judge continuity and change, a historian picks two points in time and compares them. Then they ask what is the same and what is different.
draft.remember: Compare two points in time to see what changed and what stayed the same.

a.q: Historians compare a village in 1200 with the same village in 1400. The ruler is new, but families still farm with the same tools. What does the farming show?
a.why: The farming stayed the same between the two dates, so it is continuity. The new ruler is a change, but the question asks about the farming, which did not change.
a.clue: Did the farming look different in 1400?

b.q: In 1850 a town in New South Wales had a dirt main street, a church and a blacksmith. In 1950 it had a sealed road and a petrol station, but the church was still used. Which statement is correct?
opts: The road changed, but the church shows continuity
The road and the church both show continuity
The church changed, but the road shows continuity
The road and the church both show change
b.why: The dirt street became a sealed road, so that is change. The church was still in use at both dates, so that is continuity. A town can show both at once.
b.clue: Check each item at both dates. Is it the same or different?

b.best: The road changed, but the church shows continuity
